f.title: Inform the Minister of non-fatal, non-life-threatening SUADRs within 15 days
f.statement: During the course of a clinical trial, the sponsor shall inform the Minister of any serious unexpected adverse drug reaction in respect of the drug that has occurred inside or outside Canada, if it is neither fatal nor life threatening, within 15 days after becoming aware of the information.
f.applicability: During the course of a clinical trial; serious unexpected adverse drug reactions inside or outside Canada that are neither fatal nor life threatening
f.exceptions: See HC-GUI0100-SUSAR-0004 and HC-GUI0100-SUSAR-0018 for the C.01.016/C.01.017 provisions and Phase IV trials.

deadline_rule.applies_to: Serious unexpected ADRs in a clinical trial, inside or outside Canada, neither fatal nor life threatening

f.title: Inform the Minister of fatal or life-threatening SUADRs within seven days
f.statement: During the course of a clinical trial, the sponsor shall inform the Minister of any serious unexpected adverse drug reaction in respect of the drug that has occurred inside or outside Canada, if it is fatal or life threatening, within seven days after becoming aware of the information.
f.applicability: During the course of a clinical trial; fatal or life-threatening serious unexpected adverse drug reactions inside or outside Canada
f.exceptions: See HC-GUI0100-SUSAR-0004 and HC-GUI0100-SUSAR-0018 for the C.01.016/C.01.017 provisions and Phase IV trials.

rows.deadline: Within 7 days after becoming aware of the information
rows.quote: During the course of a clinical trial, the sponsor shall inform the Minister of any serious unexpected adverse drug reaction in respect of the drug that has occurred inside or outside Canada as follows: if it is neither fatal nor life threatening, within 15 days after becoming aware of the information; and if it is fatal or life threatening, within seven days after becoming aware of the information.
rows.review_note: Review: merged HC-GUI0100-SUSAR-0011 (interpretation restating C.05.014(1)(b), true duplicate) into this regulation row; calendar days and 'first became aware' clock start taken from the interpretation. deadline_rule.applies_to: Serious unexpected ADRs in a clinical trial, inside or outside Canada, fatal or life threatening (initial notification)

f.title: Submit a complete report with assessment within eight days of the 7-day notification
f.statement: The sponsor shall, within eight days after having informed the Minister under paragraph C.05.014(1)(b) (a fatal or life-threatening serious unexpected adverse drug reaction), submit to the Minister a complete report in respect of that information that includes an assessment of the importance and implication of any findings made. The eight days run from informing the Minister, not from awareness.
f.applicability: Fatal or life-threatening serious unexpected adverse drug reactions already notified under C.05.014(1)(b)

rows.deadline: Within 8 days after informing the Minister under C.05.014(1)(b)

deadline_rule.applies_to: Complete report (with assessment) following the 7-day notification of a fatal or life-threatening SUSAR

f.title: C.01.016 and C.01.017 do not apply to clinical trial drugs
f.statement: Sections C.01.016 and C.01.017 of the Food and Drug Regulations do not apply to drugs used for the purposes of a clinical trial.
f.exceptions: Per the GUI-0100 interpretation, clinical trial drugs used in Phase IV trials remain subject to C.01.016 and C.01.017 (see HC-GUI0100-SUSAR-0018).

rows.quote: Sections C.01.016 and C.01.017 do not apply to drugs used for the purposes of a clinical trial.
rows.review_note: Review: not merged with HC-GUI0100-SUSAR-0018: the interpretation adds the Phase IV exception, which is material. Added a pointer to it under exceptions. Double-check: confirmed against the quote. Below 90: a scope provision (sections do not apply), not a duty on anyone, so the Mandatory level and sponsor actor are judgement calls; the Phase IV exception comes from another passage (row 0018).

f.title: Keep records of all AEs for the clinical trial drug, including indication and dosage form
f.statement: It is the sponsor's responsibility to keep records of all adverse events in respect of the drug used in a clinical trial, whether they occur inside or outside Canada, including information that specifies the indication for use and the dosage form of the drug at the time of the adverse event.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Data integrity & records

rows.quote: It is a sponsor's responsibility to keep records of all AEs in respect of the drug used in a clinical trial, whether those events occur inside or outside of Canada, including information that specifies the indication for use and the dosage form of the drug at the time of the AE [C.05.012(3)(c)].
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed. Below 90: 'it is a sponsor's responsibility' rather than shall/must; Mandatory rests on the cited C.05.012(3)(c), a judgement call.

f.title: QI or delegated sub-investigator to assess site AEs for seriousness, expectedness and causality
f.statement: The assessment of site adverse events for seriousness, expectedness and causality should be done by the qualified investigator (QI) or the delegated sub-investigator(s) (a physician or dentist who meets the criteria of a QI) when they become aware.

rows.quote: The assessment of the site AEs should be done by the QI or the delegated sub-investigator(s) (physician or dentist who meets the criteria of a QI) for seriousness, expectedness and causality determination, when they become aware.

f.title: QI to report all SAEs to the sponsor immediately, with a causality assessment
f.statement: Per section 2.7.2(b) of ICH E6, all serious adverse events should be reported immediately to the sponsor after the qualified investigator reasonably becomes aware of the event. The QI should also include an assessment of causality.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

rows.deadline: Immediately after the QI reasonably becomes aware of the event
rows.quote: Section 2.7.2(b) of ICH E6 states all serious adverse events (SAEs) should be reported immediately (after the QI reasonably becomes aware of the event) to the sponsor. The QI should also include an assessment of causality.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed. Below 90: the guidance restates ICH E6 2.7.2(b) ('ICH E6 states'), so the authority is another instrument rather than a Health Canada duty.

f.title: Protocol may identify SAEs that do not require immediate reporting
f.statement: In accordance with applicable regulatory requirements, the protocol may identify SAEs not requiring immediate reporting, for example deaths or other events that are endpoints.
f.applicability: SAEs identified in the protocol, such as deaths or other events that are endpoints

rows.quote: In accordance with applicable regulatory requirements, the protocol may identify SAEs not requiring immediate reporting; for example, deaths or other events that are endpoints.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed. Below 90: the protocol is the subject; the sponsor actor is inferred.

f.title: Submit subsequent SAE information as a follow-up report
f.statement: Subsequent information on a serious adverse event should be submitted as a follow-up report, as necessary.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: Subsequent information should be submitted as a follow-up report, as necessary.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed. Below 90: passive wording, so who submits follow-up (QI to sponsor) is inferred from the surrounding sentences.

f.title: Include importance, implications and relevant previous experience in fatal/life-threatening follow-up reports
f.statement: Follow-up reports of fatal or life-threatening reactions must include an assessment of the importance of the event and the implication of any findings, including relevant previous experience with the same or similar drugs.
f.applicability: Follow-up reports of fatal or life-threatening reactions

rows.quote: Follow-up reports of fatal or life-threatening reactions must include an assessment of the importance of the event and the implication of any findings, including relevant previous experience with the same or similar drugs.
data_elements: previous experience with same or similar drugs

Legal basis narrowed to C.05.014(2). Double-check: confirmed. Below 90: passive wording (sponsor inferred) and the C.05.014(2) legal basis is inferred, not cited in the quote.

f.title: Report SUSARs to QIs, institutions and REBs with appropriate urgency
f.statement: The reporting of SUSARs to qualified investigators/institutions and to research ethics boards should be undertaken in a manner that reflects the urgency of action required, should take into consideration the evolving knowledge of the safety profile of the product, and should be performed in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

rows.quote: The reporting of SUSARs to QI(s)/institutions(s) and to the REB(s) should be undertaken in a manner that reflects the urgency of action required and should take into consideration the evolving knowledge of the safety profile of the product and should be performed in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed. Below 90: passive wording; the sponsor actor is inferred.

f.title: Periodic line listings with overall safety assessment may be appropriate in some regions
f.statement: In some regions, periodic reporting of line listings with an overall safety assessment may be appropriate (ICH E6, 3.13.2(d)).

rows.quote: In some regions, periodic reporting of line listings with an overall safety assessment may be appropriate (ICH E6, 3.13.2(d)).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed against the quote. Below 90: 'in some regions ... may be appropriate' is not a clear permission under Canadian law; whether it is a requirement at all is a judgement call, and the actor is inferred.

f.title: Expedite reporting of all SUSARs to regulatory authorities per ICH E2A
f.statement: The sponsor should, in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements and with ICH E2A, expedite the reporting to the regulatory authority(ies) of all suspected, unexpected and serious adverse reactions (SUSARs).

rows.quote: The sponsor should, in accordance with the applicable regulatory requirement(s) and with ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management: Definitions and Standards for Expedited Reporting, expedite the reporting to the regulatory authority(ies) of all suspected, unexpected and serious adverse reactions (for example, SUSARs) (ICH E6, 3.13.2(b)).
rows.review_note: Review: ICH E6 'should' restatement; the binding Canadian duty is in HC-GUI0100-SUSAR-0001 to 0003. Kept as Recommended. No other change. Double-check: confirmed. Below 90: restatement of ICH E6 3.13.2(b); the binding Canadian duty is in rows 0001 to 0003.

f.title: Submit safety updates and periodic reports, including Investigator's Brochure changes
f.statement: The sponsor should submit to the regulatory authority(ies) safety updates and periodic reports, including changes to the Investigator's Brochure, as required by applicable regulatory requirements.

rows.quote: The sponsor should submit to the regulatory authority(ies) safety updates and periodic reports, including changes to the Investigator's Brochure, as required by applicable regulatory requirements (ICH E6, 3.13.2(a)).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed. Below 90: restatement of ICH E6 3.13.2(a) with no Canadian timeline.

f.title: Apply C.01.016 and C.01.017 serious ADR reporting to Phase IV trial drugs
f.statement: Sections C.01.016 and C.01.017 of the Regulations, which also refer to prohibition and serious ADR reporting, do not apply to drugs used for the purpose of a clinical trial, except clinical trial drugs used in Phase IV trials.
f.legal_basis: Food and Drug Regulations C.01.016, C.01.017

rows.actor: Clinical trial sponsor / manufacturer (Phase IV trials)
rows.quote: Sections C.01.016 and C.01.017 of the Regulations (listed below), which also refer to prohibition and serious ADR reporting, do not apply to drugs used for the purpose of a clinical trial, except clinical trial drugs used in Phase IV trials .

f.title: Do not sell a drug unless C.01.017 to C.01.019 are complied with (applies to Phase IV trial drugs)
f.statement: No manufacturer shall sell a drug unless the manufacturer complies with the conditions set out in sections C.01.017 to C.01.019.
f.applicability: Clinical trial drugs used in Phase IV trials (per HC-GUI0100-SUSAR-0018)

rows.quote: No manufacturer shall sell a drug unless the manufacturer complies with the conditions set out in sections C.01.017 to C.01.019.

f.title: Phase IV trials: report serious domestic ADRs and serious unexpected foreign ADRs within 15 days
f.statement: The manufacturer shall submit to the Minister a report of all information relating to any serious adverse drug reaction that has occurred in Canada with respect to the drug, and any serious unexpected adverse drug reaction that has occurred outside Canada with respect to the drug, within 15 days after receiving or becoming aware of the information, whichever occurs first.
f.applicability: Clinical trial drugs used in Phase IV trials (per HC-GUI0100-SUSAR-0018); serious ADRs in Canada and serious unexpected ADRs outside Canada

rows.deadline: Within 15 days after receiving or becoming aware of the information, whichever occurs first
rows.quote: The manufacturer shall submit to the Minister a report of all information relating to the following serious adverse drug reactions within 15 days after receiving or becoming aware of the information, whichever occurs first: any serious adverse drug reaction that has occurred in Canada with respect to the drug; and any serious unexpected adverse drug reaction that has occurred outside Canada with respect to the drug.
